title: Critics call it a sleeper hit: Reminisce with Chuck Green
summary: The audience and critics like the show, Nipsy Russell attends, Anna Kisselgoff writes it up, and the show is called Reminisce with Chuck Green.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Now, the audience is very happy, see. It takes right away. And then the critics started coming in there. I think there was a few critics' secretaries was there. Lot of stars was in the audience, you know, like Nipsy Russell. He's from my home state, you see. And there they call the dancing chauffeur up there now.

And one of our dancers in this show -- he's a tap dancer known as Sad Man Sims, you see. And he had one of our partner's names which was Howards. So anyhow, he did an on the town dance, Raymond Kaleland. Now the next one comes out, you see (unintelligible) see, and he does an on the town dance, you see. And that's what it was reminiscing with Chuck Green was all about on the town, you see. And that's the only kind of out of town trade and so forth and so on, see, and they was trying to keep public relations on the go at that time.

And it become what they called -- the critics finally wrote about it. They said it was a sleeper hit, you know. And this lady, Anna Kisselegoff -- I should bring you the copy of the writeup. I should have had it to you before, you know. But that's what it all consisted of, you know. And some film company was -- had some kind of apprentice, you know, a fellow named Russell Schwartz. And his staff. And they was -- had been

up to Hunter's College, you know, to show you how the spirit can move, you see. And at that time he was alive -- Professor Marshall Sterns, you see. But he was compiling. He had to be off and away, you know, him and Jean.

But they knew about it because these on-the-town dancers, you see. But we'd never tell anyone they're on-the-town dancers, you see. And -- but that's what it was based on in order to make it impressive. See, and like when they all got out there together after the first act -- see, the show was based on tap happening. And it was called "Reminisce with Chuck Green" because it was in one half -- the first part of the show which is like the first act -- the same as "Curly McDimple". Then they have the second act.
And that's when you see all these dancers like tap dancers in on-the-town dance, you see. And they each had a chance to reintroduce, you see, the remedy, see. And that's what happened, see.
